headline: Asia is crashing this morning after hot US inflation, with Korea down about **7.6%**. India looks set for a weaker start, but cheaper oil and a softer dollar should soften the blow.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: The dashboard's bias score is −35 (leaning to a fall), but only 2 of its 4 direction checks agree, so conviction is low. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: Overnight, US prices rose faster than expected in September (**3.7%** a year). The Nasdaq fell 1.9%, and Korea and Japan are down 7.6% and 4.8% this morning.
Not everything got worse: Brent crude fell **2.2%** since India closed, to $104, and the dollar and US bond rates also eased. All three help India.
My call: a weak open, then a choppy day with a slight lean lower, not a big crash. Confidence is **low**, because heavy bets on a fall could also spark a sudden bounce.
The trend is still down. Nifty at 22,623 is below its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages, and foreign funds (FIIs) have sold for **7 days** in a row.
Domestic funds (DIIs) bought ₹2,670 crore yesterday, more than the **₹1,857 crore** FIIs sold. That is why falls have stayed small.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night brought worse news for stocks, mostly through Asia's crash, so it supports yesterday's small fall, though oil and the dollar moved India's way.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (the overnight Nifty contract) was around 22,580–22,610 early this morning, slightly below Nifty's close of 22,623. Sources differ on the exact figure, but they all **point to a weaker open**.
Asia is falling hard: Korea is down **7.6%**, Japan 4.8% and Taiwan 3.1%, led by chip and AI stocks, which India has few of.
US stocks fell yesterday (S&P 500 −1.1%, Nasdaq −1.9%) after the hot inflation report. Nasdaq futures are down another **1.0%** since India closed.
Brent crude fell **2.2%** since India closed, to $104, and the dollar index fell 0.6%. India imports most of its oil, so both help.
The US 10-year bond rate fell about **0.09 points** to 5.10%. Lower US rates make it less tempting for foreign money to leave India.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: My read is mild continuation today: a weak start and a slightly lower day, with low confidence because the setup for a sharp bounce is also there.

points.text: For continuation: fresh bad news overnight (US inflation, Asia crash), a trend that is negative on every check, and FIIs who **added more bets on a fall** in index futures yesterday.
For a bounce: only **9.4%** of FII index-futures positions are bets on a rise. Below 10% has often come before a rush to close bets on a fall, and VIX is flat, not panicking.
Also for a bounce: FII selling yesterday (₹1,857 crore) was well below their recent daily average of about ₹4,768 crore, and **DIIs bought more** than FIIs sold.
What would prove me wrong: Nifty holding above 22,623 after the first hour while Asia stays weak. That would suggest buyers are absorbing the bad news and a **bounce is under way**.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The data shows a market in a downtrend, close to its recent lows, with mixed signals from the option market.

points.text: Nifty at 22,623 is below its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages, and recent peaks and dips are both lower. The price trend scores the **lowest possible: −2**.
Prices fell yesterday while futures positions grew slightly, which usually means **new bets on a fall** (step score −1.1).
Options traders bought calls (bets on a rise) at 22,700–23,000, which the dashboard reads as **mildly positive (+0.3)**. The put-call ratio of 0.91 is neutral (0).

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign funds keep selling and betting on a fall, but domestic funds are buying even more in the cash market.

points.text: FIIs sold ₹1,857 crore of shares yesterday, their **7th selling day** in a row. They have sold ₹30,466 crore so far in October.
DIIs (Indian mutual funds, insurers) bought ₹2,670 crore yesterday and **₹33,287 crore** this month, more than all of the FII selling.
FIIs hold about 3.3 lakh index-futures contracts betting on a fall vs 34,000 on a rise, and added more yesterday. If news improves, they may **close those bets in a hurry**.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: US inflation is the main worry: it makes another US rate rise more likely, which tends to pull money out of countries like India.

points.text: US prices rose 3.7% in a year in September, above the 3.6% expected. Reports put the chance of a **Fed rate rise this month** at about 33–40%, up from about 22% before the data.
The dashboard flags that 6-month US Treasury bills pay 4.37%, **0.49 points above** the Fed's rate. This means the market expects the Fed to raise rates.
Oil is still high at $104, up 18% in 3 months on Middle East supply worries. The dashboard's overall reading of the world backdrop is **Mixed**.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: The main IT results so far were solid, while yesterday's filings were a mix of strong and weak.

points.text: HCL Tech (a Nifty 50 company) reported profit up **21%** and revenue up 11.5% from last year. IT shares rallied this week after TCS and HCL.
Infosys's US-listed shares rose 0.4% since India closed and Wipro's rose 0.6%. This suggests **IT is holding up**, even as US tech fell.
Yesterday's filings were split: BHEL (profit **+119%**) and MRPL were strong, while CEAT (−40%) was weak and Crompton made a loss. Big banks report on Saturday.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: US data tonight, a Fed chair speech tomorrow morning, and the big bank results this weekend are the main tests.

points.text: Tonight at 6 pm IST: US retail sales and producer prices. Another **hot number** would raise rate-rise fears again and hurt markets.
Tomorrow at 9 am IST, Fed chair Warsh speaks, just before the market opens. A **firm tone on raising rates** would be bad for India; a calm one could help a bounce.
HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank report on 17 October; the Fed decides around midnight on 28–29 October. A rise in FIIs' long % of **3 points or more** would flip the dashboard's step 2.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 (the biggest call wall) would suggest bets on a fall are being closed; a close below 22,500 (the biggest put wall) would open the way to the recent lows near 22,200.

watch.text: The open: does Nifty open near GIFT Nifty's 22,580–22,610, and does it hold 22,500?
Korea and Japan through the day. A recovery there would ease pressure on India.
Today's FII and DII cash figures, published in the evening. Watch whether DIIs keep buying more than FIIs sell.
US retail sales and producer prices. Hot numbers would revive US rate-rise fears.

bottom_line: The data shows a downtrend: Nifty is below all its averages, FIIs keep selling and adding bets on a fall, and the night brought hot US inflation and a crash in Asia. My read is a weak, choppy session with a slight lean lower, but with low confidence: the dashboard's checks only partly agree, cheaper oil and a weaker dollar help India, and domestic funds keep buying. The main risk to this read is a sudden bounce: FIIs have very few bets on a rise (9.4%), so any good news could force them to close their bets on a fall quickly.
